title: HCLTech Acquires Guardian India for $10.5 Million in AI-Led Transformation Deal
excerpt: Nearly 2,000 employees will transition to HCLTech under a seven-year partnership aimed at modernizing Guardian Life Insurance's technology operations with AI.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • HCLTech acquires 100% of Guardian India Operations for $10.5 million
  • Nearly 2,000 employees will transition to HCLTech under the deal
  • Seven-year AI partnership will deploy HCLTech's AI Force platform for Guardian Life Insurance

Indian IT major HCLTech has announced the acquisition of Guardian India Operations for $10.5 million (approximately ₹101 crore), a deal that will see nearly 2,000 employees of the U.S.-based insurer transition to the tech giant under a seven-year strategic partnership focused on AI-driven transformation.

The Deal Structure

Under the agreement, HCLTech will acquire a 100% stake in the entity, which serves as the technology and operations Global Capability Centre (GCC) for Guardian Life Insurance Company of America — one of the largest U.S. life insurers and a major provider of employee benefits, retirement, and wealth management solutions.

Guardian India, incorporated in March 2002, reported revenue of ₹578.8 crore in FY26, up from ₹483.2 crore in FY25. The transaction is expected to be completed by August 1, 2026.

Karunakaran Azhisur, currently the Country Head of Guardian India, will join HCLTech to lead the new Strategic Business Unit focused exclusively on supporting Guardian.

AI at the Center

The seven-year partnership aims to advance Guardian's AI-powered modernization across technology and operations. HCLTech will expand the use of its AI service transformation platform, AI Force, to create and deploy agentic capabilities for Guardian's enterprise-wide operations.

"We are excited to welcome the talented team joining us from Guardian. Together, we have a unique opportunity to partner to co-create products and intellectual property that will deepen HCLTech's domain expertise, further strengthen our AI-intrinsic platforms and help clients achieve sustained business growth," said Srinivasan Seshadri, Chief Growth Officer and Global Head of Financial Services at HCLTech.

Steve Rullo, Guardian's chief digital and technology officer, described the partnership as "a key step in our long-term strategy to harness data and AI, consolidate services with a single strategic partner and modernize our core technology foundations."

HCLTech's AI Momentum

The acquisition comes as HCLTech continues to build its AI-led services portfolio. The company recently reported that AI is deployed across 92 client accounts, with its AI Force platform receiving a 2.2 update that added multimodal AI and long-term memory features. HCLTech now offers 23 industry-specific AI solutions and has completed more than 1,000 AI engagements.

CEO C. Vijayakumar has outlined a five-pillar AI strategy: transforming services with AI, building differentiated IP, expanding AI-led services, scaling AI partnerships, and developing AI talent. The company also announced a $150 million investment in Sarvam, an Indian sovereign AI company, during its latest quarter.

Implications for Indian Tech Workers

The deal reinforces the pattern of Indian IT services companies absorbing GCCs of multinational clients — a model that creates stable employment pathways for Indian tech professionals while giving U.S. firms access to AI and digital engineering capabilities at scale. For the nearly 2,000 transitioning employees, the move to HCLTech offers a larger career platform within one of India's top IT services firms.
